headline: The Ranch & Cowboy Master 20
threshold: By Lesson 20, you can train a new hand and have them teach it back, explain a problem and a proposal to the owner or a client, settle a crew conflict, report an incident or near miss without blame, and write the day's ranch report in Spanish.

lessons.title: Teach a New Hand the Flight Zone and Why It Works
lessons.objective: Explain low-stress cattle handling step by step and why it works, then have the new hand teach it back.

words.note: The space an animal keeps clear around itself; step into it and the animal moves away.
Common in Mexico for the edge of a zone, field or road.
Changes its ending to match the noun: -o, -a, -os, -as.

words.en: First you stand at the edge of the flight zone.
words.es: Primero te paras en la orilla de la zona de fuga.
words.note: Informal tú, foreman to a new hand.

words.en: Then you move behind the shoulder and the animal moves forward.
words.es: Luego te mueves detrás del hombro y el animal avanza.

words.en: When it walks, you release the pressure, because that's its reward.
words.es: Cuando camina, sueltas la presión, porque ese es su premio.

words.en: We don't yell, because scared cattle bunch up.
words.es: No gritamos, porque el ganado asustado se amontona.

words.en: That's why we work slow and calm.
words.es: Por eso trabajamos despacio y tranquilos.

words.en: Don't stand in its blind spot, because it can kick you.
words.es: No te pongas en su punto ciego, porque te puede patear.

words.en: Why does the cow stop when you come in from the front?
words.es: ¿Por qué se detiene la vaca cuando entras de frente?

words.en: Now you explain it to me, step by step.
words.es: Ahora explícamelo tú, paso por paso.

lessons.speaking: You are the foreman, and the AI is Mateo, a new hand used to yelling at cattle: explain pressure and release step by step with primero, luego and después, give the reasons with porque and por eso, then have him teach it back to you.

grammar.focus: Connectors for sequence and cause (primero, luego, después, porque, por eso)

examples.es: Primero te acercas despacio, y luego te detienes en la orilla.
examples.en: First you approach slowly, and then you stop at the edge.

examples.es: Los gritos asustan al ganado; por eso se amontona en el portón.
examples.en: Yelling scares the cattle; that's why they bunch up at the gate.

lessons.title: Reading the Feed Bunk Before the Morning Ration
lessons.objective: Explain how bunks are scored each morning and what is done when cattle leave feed or lick the bunk clean.

words.note: Bunk licked bare; you note it and report it before changing anything.
Very common ranch word for evenly spread or consistent.

words.en: The bunk gets checked before loading the truck.
words.es: Se revisa el comedero antes de cargar el camión.

words.en: If the bunk is licked clean, the foreman gets told.
words.es: Si el comedero está lamido, se le avisa al capataz.

words.en: If there's feed left over, the ration goes down.
words.es: Si queda sobrante, se baja la ración.

words.en: Here nobody dumps extra feed without asking.
words.es: Aquí no se echa alimento extra sin preguntar.

words.en: What score would you give this bunk?
words.es: ¿Qué calificación le pones a este comedero?
words.note: Informal tú, to a coworker.

words.en: If you raise the ration all at once, they can get acidosis.
words.es: Si subes la ración de golpe, les puede dar acidosis.

words.en: Write it on the bunk sheet, please.
words.es: Anótalo en la hoja de comederos, por favor.

words.en: Sir, do you approve the increase for pen 12?
words.es: Señor, ¿autoriza el aumento para el corral 12?
words.note: Formal usted, to the manager or owner.

lessons.speaking: You are the foreman, and the AI is Nicolás, the new feed-truck driver: teach him how bunks are scored each morning and what is done with leftover feed or licked-clean bunks, using impersonal se and si + present (si está limpio, se avisa).

grammar.focus: Impersonal se; si + present for general truths (se revisa el comedero; si está limpio, se avisa)

examples.es: Se lee cada comedero a la misma hora todas las mañanas.
examples.en: Each bunk is read at the same time every morning.

examples.es: Si el comedero está vacío, se anota y se avisa.
examples.en: If the bunk is empty, it gets written down and reported.

lessons.title: Saddling Up: Training a New Rider on Cinch Checks
lessons.objective: Give clear step-by-step commands to saddle a horse and check the cinch, then hear the rider repeat them.

words.note: On a saddle, the strap that tightens the cinch, not a whip.
Many Mexican ranch hands also say cabresto.
Ranch hands often call a horse by its coat color, such as gray or sorrel.

words.en: Put the pad on first, centered on the withers.
words.es: Ponle el sudadero primero, centrado en la cruz.
words.note: Informal tú, foreman to a new rider.

words.en: Tighten it little by little; don't cinch it all at once.
words.es: Ajústala poco a poco; no la aprietes de golpe.

words.en: Walk him a few steps and check it again.
words.es: Camínalo unos pasos y revísala otra vez.

words.en: He holds his breath, that's why the cinch loosens.
words.es: Él aguanta el aire, por eso la cincha se afloja.

words.en: Don't skip it; the second check always gets done.
words.es: No te la saltes; la segunda revisión siempre se hace.

words.en: Does a flat hand fit under the cinch?
words.es: ¿Cabe la mano plana debajo de la cincha?

words.note: Formal usted, to the owner's relative or a guest rider.

words.en: Now you tell me: what do you do first?

lessons.speaking: You are the foreman, and the AI is Daniela, a nervous new rider: walk her through saddling the gray gelding and both cinch checks with commands like ajústala, revísala and no la aprietes de golpe, then have her repeat the steps back to you.

grammar.focus: Commands with object pronouns (ajústala, revísalo, no la aprietes de golpe)

examples.es: Apriétala un poco y luego revísala otra vez.
examples.en: Tighten it a little, then check it again.

examples.es: No la aprietes de golpe; súbela de a poco.
examples.en: Don't tighten it all at once; bring it up a little at a time.

lessons.title: Read the Pour-On Label Before Treating the Heifers
lessons.objective: Read a pour-on label aloud and explain dose by weight, withdrawal time and protective gear as the label states.

words.note: Common Mexican word for the slaughterhouse.

words.en: Before applying, you have to read the whole label.
words.es: Antes de aplicar, hay que leer la etiqueta completa.

words.en: Don't guess the weight; we have to weigh them one by one.
words.es: No adivines el peso; hay que pesarlas una por una.
words.note: Informal tú, to a coworker.

words.en: According to the label, the dose depends on each animal's weight.
words.es: Según la etiqueta, la dosis depende del peso de cada animal.

words.en: Put on the gloves and glasses before opening the container.
words.es: Ponte los guantes y los lentes antes de abrir el envase.

words.en: How many withdrawal days does the label require before slaughter?
words.es: ¿Cuántos días de retiro pide la etiqueta antes del rastro?

words.en: After applying, you have to wash your hands with soap.
words.es: Después de aplicar, hay que lavarse las manos con jabón.

words.en: If you have a doubt, we stop and ask the vet.
words.es: Si tienes duda, paramos y le preguntamos al veterinario.

words.en: Don Ramón, would you like to check the records before we turn them out?
words.es: Don Ramón, ¿quiere revisar las anotaciones antes de soltarlas?
words.note: Formal usted, to the owner.

lessons.speaking: You are the foreman, and the AI is Rogelio, a ranch hand: read the pour-on label aloud with him and explain dose by weight, withdrawal time and protective gear as la etiqueta dice, using antes de / después de + infinitive and hay que.

grammar.focus: Antes de / después de + infinitive; hay que (antes de aplicar, hay que leer la etiqueta)

examples.es: Antes de aplicar, hay que pesar cada novilla.
examples.en: Before applying, you have to weigh each heifer.

examples.es: Después de terminar, hay que guardar el envase bien cerrado.
examples.en: After finishing, you have to store the container tightly closed.

lessons.title: Larkspur in the North Lease: Move the Herd Early
lessons.objective: Tell the owner what you found in the pasture and propose moving the cows early, answering his worry about cost.

words.note: Poisonous to cattle. Tall larkspur is most dangerous before and during flowering.
Common ranch word for a patch of plants or weeds.
Common Mexican word for freight or the cost of hauling.
The ending changes to -a when you talk about a cow or heifer.

words.en: When I got there, the cows were eating in the patch.
words.es: Cuando llegué, las vacas estaban comiendo en el manchón.
words.note: Preterite for the moment you arrived, imperfect for the background action.

words.en: The larkspur was already flowering by the creek.
words.es: La espuela de caballero ya estaba en flor junto al arroyo.

words.en: I didn't see sick animals, but they were biting the plant.
words.es: No vi animales enfermos, pero sí estaban mordiendo la planta.

words.en: With all due respect, Don Esteban, I wouldn't wait a week.
words.es: Con todo respeto, Don Esteban, yo no esperaría una semana.
words.note: Formal and polite way to disagree with the owner.

words.en: I would move them to the reserve pasture this week.
words.es: Yo las movería al potrero de reserva esta semana.

words.en: One dead cow would cost us more than the hauling.
words.es: Una vaca muerta nos costaría más que el flete.

words.en: Meanwhile, we could fence off the patch with electric wire.
words.es: Mientras tanto, podríamos cercar el manchón con alambre eléctrico.

words.en: Would it be all right with you if we started early tomorrow?
words.es: ¿Le parecería bien que empezáramos mañana temprano?
words.note: Formal. Conditional + que + past subjunctive.

lessons.speaking: You are the foreman, and the AI is Don Esteban Villarreal, the owner: tell him what you found in the north lease with the preterite and imperfect (cuando llegué, estaban comiendo), and propose moving the herd early with the conditional (sería mejor, nos costaría menos).

grammar.focus: Preterite vs imperfect; conditional for the proposal (cuando llegué, las vacas estaban comiendo; sería mejor moverlas)

examples.es: Cuando llegué, las vacas estaban comiendo espuela de caballero.
examples.en: When I got there, the cows were eating larkspur.

examples.es: Sería mejor moverlas antes del sábado.
examples.en: It would be better to move them before Saturday.

lessons.title: Hay Delivery Comes Up Short: Cubes Instead of Bales
lessons.objective: Work out a feed substitution with the dealer, compare options on cost and quantity, and plan the next weeks.

words.note: Ranchers often just say los cubos.
Crop residue left in the field after the corn harvest.

words.en: So only half of the alfalfa is going to arrive?
words.es: Entonces, ¿solo va a llegar la mitad de la alfalfa?

words.en: The cubes are going to cost more than the hay, right?
words.es: Los cubos van a costar más que el heno, ¿verdad?

words.en: The corn stalks are cheaper, but they have less protein than the cubes.
words.es: El rastrojo es más barato, pero tiene menos proteína que los cubos.

words.en: How many tons of cubes can you have for me by Friday?
words.es: ¿Cuántas toneladas de cubos me puede tener para el viernes?
words.note: Formal: usted with the dealer.

words.en: With the cold front, the cows will eat more than they do now.
words.es: Con el frente frío, las vacas comerán más que ahora.

words.en: I'll take half in cubes and the other half in corn stalks.
words.es: Llevaré la mitad en cubos y la otra mitad en rastrojo.

words.en: When will the rest of the order arrive?
I'll confirm with you this afternoon, after I talk to the boss.
words.es: Le confirmo hoy en la tarde, después de hablar con el patrón.
words.note: Formal. El patrón is the usual word for the ranch owner or boss.

lessons.speaking: You are the foreman, and the AI is Graciela Montoya, the feed dealer at the co-op: work out a substitute for the missing alfalfa, compare cubes and corn stalks with más que / menos que, and plan the next weeks with the future and ir a.

grammar.focus: Future and ir a; comparisons (los cubos van a costar más que el heno; durarán menos)

examples.es: Los cubos van a costar más que el heno.
examples.en: The cubes are going to cost more than the hay.

examples.es: El rastrojo durará menos que la alfalfa.
examples.en: The corn stalks won't last as long as the alfalfa.

lessons.title: Brand Inspector at the Pens: Three Pairs Missing
lessons.objective: Explain to a brand inspector what happened during the gather and give exact counts and brands under pressure.

words.note: Cow-calf pairs: each pair is one cow with her calf.
Small pasture next to the pens, used to hold cattle before working them.
On a ranch this means the roundup or gather, not the sport.
Feminine noun that takes el in the singular, like el agua.

words.en: We counted 147 pairs in the pen, and the papers say 150.
words.es: Contamos 147 pares en el corral y los papeles dicen 150.

words.en: Three pairs broke back into the trap through the gap.
words.es: Tres pares se regresaron a la trampa por el hueco.

words.en: They broke back on us while we were closing the gate.
words.es: Se nos regresaron cuando estábamos cerrando la puerta.

words.en: All three cows carry our brand on the left hip.
words.es: Las tres vacas traen nuestra marca en el anca izquierda.

words.en: They're two reds and one black, with their calves.
words.es: Son dos coloradas y una negra, con sus becerros.

words.en: Mr. Carrillo, here are the tag numbers for all three.
words.es: Señor Carrillo, aquí tiene los números de arete de las tres.
words.note: Formal: usted with the inspector.

words.en: I already sent two cowboys to the trap for them.
words.es: Ya mandé a dos vaqueros por ellas a la trampa.
words.note: Use the personal a before people as the direct object.

words.en: Do you want us to do the recount together when they get here?
words.es: ¿Quiere que hagamos el recuento juntos cuando lleguen?
words.note: Formal.

lessons.speaking: You are the foreman, and the AI is Luis Carrillo, the brand inspector: explain in the preterite what happened during the gather (contamos, se regresaron), give exact counts, brands and tag numbers, and agree with him on how to finish the count.

grammar.focus: Preterite narration; numbers under pressure (contamos 147, tres pares se regresaron a la trampa)

examples.es: Contamos 147 pares y tres se regresaron a la trampa.
examples.en: We counted 147 pairs, and three broke back into the trap.

examples.es: A las 9:30 cerramos el último corral y contamos otra vez.
examples.en: At 9:30 we closed the last pen and counted again.

lessons.title: Saying No: The Trucker Wants to Load a Lame Cow
lessons.objective: Refuse to load an unfit cow, explain why calmly and firmly, and offer what you will do instead.

words.note: Common US Mexican word for a semi or trailer driver.
The adjective ending agrees with the animal (apto for a steer, apta for a cow).
Only the vet makes this call.

words.en: Armando, don't load her; she won't put weight on her hind leg.
words.es: Armando, no la subas; no apoya la pata trasera.
words.note: Informal tú, as between two working men who know each other.

words.en: I don't recommend that we load her like this.
words.es: No recomiendo que la carguemos así.
words.note: No recomiendo que + subjunctive.

words.en: If she goes down in the trailer, the others trample her.
words.es: Si se cae en la jaula, las otras la pisan.

words.en: Don't drive her to the chute; leave her in the sick pen.
words.es: No la arrees al embarcadero; déjala en el corral de enfermería.
words.note: Informal.

words.en: I already called the vet; he decides if she can travel.
words.es: Ya llamé al veterinario; él decide si puede viajar.

words.en: Load the rest, and this one stays until he checks her.
words.es: Carga las demás, y esta se queda hasta que la revise.
words.note: Informal. Hasta que + subjunctive for a future event.

words.en: I understand you're in a hurry, but this one doesn't get on.
words.es: Entiendo que traes prisa, pero esta no se sube.
words.note: Informal. Traer prisa is common Mexican usage.

words.en: Doctor, can you come today to check a lame cow?
words.es: Doctor, ¿puede venir hoy a revisar una vaca coja?
words.note: Formal: usted with the vet.

lessons.speaking: You are the foreman, and the AI is Armando Leyva, the cull-cow trucker: calmly refuse to load the lame cow using negative commands (no la subas) and no recomiendo que + subjunctive, explain why, and offer what you will do instead, including calling the vet.

grammar.focus: Negative commands; subjunctive after no recomiendo que (no la subas; no recomiendo que la carguemos)

examples.es: No la subas a la jaula, Armando.
examples.en: Don't load her onto the trailer, Armando.

examples.es: No recomiendo que la carguemos sin la revisión veterinaria.
examples.en: I don't recommend that we load her without the vet check.

lessons.title: Feedback on Rough Sorting: Show Me How You'd Do It
lessons.objective: Give a young hand specific feedback on sorting technique and have him teach back the better way.

words.note: A group of animals worked together at one time.
Here, the signal you give the person working the gate.
Same form for a man or a woman: él es paciente, ella es paciente.

words.en: Kevin, you're rushing and splitting cows from their calves.
words.es: Kevin, vas muy apurado y estás separando vacas de sus crías.
words.note: Informal: tú with a young hand.

words.en: I want you to stand near the sort gate.
words.es: Quiero que te pares cerca de la puerta de aparte.
words.note: Quiero que + subjunctive: te pares, not te paras.

words.en: I recommend you wait for the calf to go through with its mother.
words.es: Te recomiendo que esperes a que la cría pase con su mamá.

words.en: I don't want you to bunch them up against the fence.
words.es: No quiero que las amontones contra la cerca.

words.en: I'd rather you work slower with each bunch.
words.es: Prefiero que trabajes más lento con cada tanda.

words.en: I want you to give me a heads-up before you send each animal.
words.es: Quiero que me avises antes de mandar cada animal.

words.en: You sorted the last three really well.
words.es: Las últimas tres las apartaste muy bien.

words.en: Okay, show me how you're going to sort the next bunch.
words.es: A ver, enséñame cómo vas a apartar la siguiente tanda.

lessons.speaking: You are the foreman, and the AI is Kevin, a young hand who rushes the heifers: give him specific feedback on his sorting with quiero que… and te recomiendo que…, then have him teach back how he'll sort the next bunch.

grammar.focus: Present subjunctive after wishes and recommendations (quiero que te pares aquí; te recomiendo que esperes)

examples.es: Quiero que abras la puerta solo cuando yo te avise.
examples.en: I want you to open the gate only when I tell you.

examples.es: Te recomiendo que muevas la bandera despacio.
examples.en: I recommend that you move the flag slowly.

lessons.title: Who Left the Gate Open? Settling It Between Two Hands
lessons.objective: Hear both sides of a crew conflict, report what each one said, and agree on a fair plan going forward.

words.note: Un plan justo = a fair plan; justa for a feminine noun: una decisión justa.

words.en: I'm not looking for someone to blame; I want to know what happened.
words.es: No estoy buscando culpables; quiero saber qué pasó.

words.en: One at a time; first I'll listen to you, Paco.
words.es: Uno a la vez; primero te escucho a ti, Paco.
words.note: Informal: tú between foreman and hand.

words.en: Raúl, what time did you leave and how was the gate?
words.es: Raúl, ¿a qué hora saliste y cómo estaba la puerta?

words.en: Paco said the chain was on when he left the pasture.
words.es: Paco dijo que la cadena estaba puesta cuando salió del potrero.
words.note: Reported speech: dijo que + imperfect (estaba) for the situation at that moment.

words.en: Raúl said he hadn't gone through that gate.
words.es: Raúl dijo que él no había pasado por esa puerta.

words.en: Starting today, the last one through puts the chain on.
words.es: Desde hoy, el último que pase pone la cadena.

words.en: Do you both agree with this plan?
words.es: ¿Están de acuerdo los dos con este plan?

words.en: Now, both of you together, get the bulls out of that pasture.
words.es: Ahora, los dos juntos, saquen los toros de ese potrero.
words.note: Saquen is the ustedes command, for two or more people.

lessons.speaking: You are the foreman, and the AI plays the two hands, Paco and Raúl: hear each side, report back what each one said with dijo que… and the imperfect (estaba, había), and agree on a fair gate plan before lunch.

grammar.focus: Reported speech; imperfect for background (Paco dijo que la puerta estaba cerrada cuando él salió)

examples.es: Raúl me dijo que ya estaba oscuro y no vio la puerta.
examples.en: Raúl told me it was already dark and he didn't see the gate.

examples.es: Paco explicó que el pasador ya estaba flojo.
examples.en: Paco explained that the latch was already loose.

lessons.title: Keeping the Crew Going Through a Blizzard Calving Week
lessons.objective: Encourage a tired crew, make concrete commitments about shifts and rest, and keep night checks going.

words.note: El rol is common Mexican usage for a rotating schedule.
The person who takes over your shift, or the handover itself.
Agotada for a woman: Marisol está agotada.

words.en: I know you're exhausted, and you're right.
words.es: Sé que están agotados, y tienen razón.

words.en: Héctor, tomorrow you'll sleep six hours; I'll do your check.
words.es: Héctor, mañana dormirás seis horas; yo haré tu revisión.
words.note: Future for a firm promise: dormirás, haré.

words.en: Tonight you'll get relief at 2 a.m.
words.es: Esta noche tendrás relevo a las 2 de la mañana.

words.en: On Saturday a cowboy from the neighboring ranch will come to help.
words.es: El sábado llegará un vaquero del rancho vecino para ayudar.

words.en: When the storm passes, each of you will get a day off.
words.es: Cuando pase la tormenta, cada uno tendrá un día libre.
words.note: Cuando + subjunctive (pase) for a future moment.

words.en: Héctor, I don't want to lose you; tell me what you need to stay.
words.es: Héctor, no quiero perderte; dime qué necesitas para quedarte.

words.en: Marisol, you saved that calf last night; good job.
words.es: Marisol, salvaste a ese becerro anoche; buen trabajo.

words.en: We'll get through this together; only a few cows left.
words.es: Saldremos adelante juntos; ya faltan pocas vacas.

lessons.speaking: You are the foreman, and the AI plays the tired hands Marisol, Héctor and Teo: recognize their effort, make concrete promises about shifts and rest with the future (dormirás, tendrás, haremos), answer Héctor, and keep the night checks going.

grammar.focus: Future for commitments; encouragement register (mañana dormirás seis horas; lo lograremos juntos)

examples.es: Mañana te tocará descansar toda la tarde.
examples.en: Tomorrow you'll get to rest all afternoon.

examples.es: Yo me quedaré en el establo esta noche.
examples.en: I'll stay in the barn tonight.

lessons.title: Preg-Check Day: Vet, Owner and Crew in One Alley
lessons.objective: Switch between usted and tú with the vet, the owner and a young hand, using softeners with each listener.

words.note: Used for cows; for a woman say embarazada.
Often shortened to la trico on ranches.
Common US and northern Mexico loanword.
Ranch crews address a vet as doctora or doctor.
Say it when you step past someone or interrupt politely.

words.en: Doctor, could you check cow 214 again?
words.es: Doctora, ¿podría usted revisar otra vez la vaca 214?
words.note: Formal: ¿podría usted…? softens a request.

words.en: I'd like to know how far along this one is, please.
words.es: Quisiera saber cuántos meses tiene esta, por favor.
words.note: Formal: quisiera sounds more polite than quiero.

words.en: Mrs. Hallorán, I understand your concern about the open cows.
words.es: Señora Hallorán, entiendo su preocupación por las vacas vacías.
words.note: Formal: su preocupación, for usted.

words.en: Would it be okay if the doctor explains the possible causes to you?
words.es: ¿Le parece si la doctora le explica las posibles causas?
words.note: Formal.

words.en: Ma'am, would you like to look at the results with me at the truck?
words.es: Señora, ¿quisiera ver los resultados conmigo en la troca?
words.note: Formal.

words.en: Hey, Joaquín, hand me the paint stick and the clipboard.
words.es: Oye, Joaquín, pásame el crayón y el portapapeles.
words.note: Informal: oye and pásame with a young hand.

words.en: Mark her with a stripe on the hip, please.
words.es: Márcala con una raya en el anca, porfa.
words.note: Informal: porfa is a casual por favor.

words.en: Joaquín, write down the tag number and the months for me.
words.es: Joaquín, apúntame el número de arete y los meses.
words.note: Informal.

lessons.speaking: You are the foreman, and the AI plays Dra. Lozano, owner Sra. Hallorán and young hand Joaquín: keep the preg check moving, using usted and softeners (quisiera, ¿podría usted…?) with the vet and the owner, and tú (oye, pásame) with Joaquín.

grammar.focus: Usted / tú switching; softeners (quisiera, ¿podría usted…?, oye, pásame)

examples.es: Señora, quisiera mostrarle los números de la doctora.
examples.en: Ma'am, I'd like to show you the doctor's numbers.

examples.es: Oye, Joaquín, pásale un guante nuevo a la doctora.
examples.en: Hey, Joaquín, hand the doctor a new sleeve.

lessons.title: Horse Wreck on the East Hillside: Injury Report
lessons.objective: Narrate an injury in time order and complete the incident report for the owner and the insurer.

words.note: Reporte is the usual word in Mexico and the US.
Use la testigo for a woman.
Use adolorida for a woman.

words.en: At 9:15 we were coming down the east hillside with the cattle.
words.es: A las 9:15 bajábamos por la ladera este con el ganado.

words.en: While we were coming down, Arturo's horse stepped in a hole.
words.es: Mientras bajábamos, el caballo de Arturo metió la pata en un hoyo.
words.note: Imperfect (bajábamos) sets the scene; preterite (metió) is the event.

words.en: At that moment, the horse went down on its nose and Arturo fell.
words.es: En ese momento, el caballo se fue de boca y Arturo cayó.

words.en: Shortly after, we put a sling on him and drove him down in the truck.
words.es: Poco después, le pusimos un cabestrillo y lo bajamos en la troca.

words.en: At 10:30 we got to the emergency room.
words.es: A las 10:30 llegamos a la sala de emergencias.

words.en: Arturo, did you hit your head when you fell?
words.es: Arturo, ¿te pegaste en la cabeza cuando caíste?
words.note: Informal, to a coworker.

words.en: Mr. Treviño, here is the report for the insurance company.
words.es: Señor Treviño, aquí tiene el reporte para la aseguradora.
words.note: Formal, to the owner.

lessons.speaking: You are the foreman, and the AI is owner Samuel Treviño: tell him what happened in the wreck in time order for the incident report, using time markers like a las 9:15, mientras bajábamos, en ese momento and poco después, and answer his questions for the insurer.

grammar.focus: Past narration with time markers (a las 9:15, poco después, mientras bajábamos, en ese momento)

examples.es: A las 9:15, mientras bajábamos por la ladera, el caballo tropezó.
examples.en: At 9:15, while we were coming down the hillside, the horse stumbled.

examples.es: Poco después, Arturo dijo que le dolía mucho el hombro.
examples.en: Shortly after, Arturo said his shoulder hurt a lot.

lessons.title: Near Miss: A Protective Cow Charges at Tagging
lessons.objective: Talk through a near miss without blame, describe what could have happened, and agree on changes.

words.en: Nobody is to blame here; we want to learn from this.
words.es: Aquí nadie tiene la culpa; queremos aprender de esto.

words.en: Rosa, the cow almost got you.
words.es: Rosa, por poco te alcanza la vaca.
words.note: Por poco + present tense describes something that almost happened.

words.en: If the cow had reached you, you could have ended up in the hospital.
words.es: Si la vaca te hubiera alcanzado, podrías haber terminado en el hospital.

words.en: Fidel, what did you see from the gate when the cow charged?
words.es: Fidel, ¿qué viste desde la puerta cuando la vaca embistió?
words.note: Informal, to a coworker.

words.en: If we had used the vehicle, Rosa would have had a barrier.
words.es: Si hubiéramos usado el vehículo, Rosa habría tenido una barrera.

words.en: We're not going to tag on foot anymore without someone watching.
words.es: Ya no vamos a aretear a pie sin nadie vigilando.
words.note: After sin, Spanish uses nadie, not alguien.

words.en: What would you change for next time?
words.es: ¿Qué cambiarían ustedes para la próxima vez?

words.en: Something serious almost happened; I'm glad you're okay.
words.es: Casi nos pasa algo serio; qué bueno que estás bien.

lessons.speaking: You are the foreman, and the AI is Rosa Elizondo, who was nearly run down while tagging: talk it through without blame, describe what could have happened with por poco and podría haber, and agree on changes using si hubiéramos… habría…

grammar.focus: Casi, por poco, podría haber; si clauses (por poco te alcanza; si hubiéramos usado el vehículo…)

examples.es: Por poco te alcanza; casi te tumba junto al becerro.
examples.en: She almost got you; she nearly knocked you down next to the calf.

examples.es: Si hubiéramos usado el vehículo, la vaca no habría llegado hasta ti.
examples.en: If we had used the vehicle, the cow wouldn't have reached you.

lessons.title: Lightning Over the Gather: Radio Call to Stop Work
lessons.objective: Stop a gather by radio with short clear commands and plan where each rider goes if the storm gets closer.

words.note: In the Southwest, a flat-topped high area of land.
Common in Mexico for a sudden rise in an arroyo.
Said at the end of a radio message.

words.en: Benito, Lupe, leave the cattle and stop now!
words.es: ¡Benito, Lupe, dejen el ganado y paren ya!
words.note: Ustedes command to the riders.

words.en: Get off your horses now and get off the ridge!
words.es: ¡Desmonten ya y bajen de la cresta!

words.note: Radio usage, informal.

words.en: If you hear thunder, you'll go down to low ground, away from the arroyo.
words.es: Si escuchas truenos, bajarás al terreno bajo, lejos del arroyo.

words.en: If you don't answer in 2 minutes, Benito will go look for you.
words.es: Si no contestas en 2 minutos, Benito irá a buscarte.

words.en: Benito, if the storm gets closer, you'll go straight to the truck.
words.es: Benito, si la tormenta se acerca, irás directo a la troca.

words.en: Get away from the fence and the lone trees.
words.es: Aléjense de la cerca y de los árboles aislados.

words.en: Don't bunch up; stay spread out from each other.
words.es: No se junten; quédense separados unos de otros.

lessons.speaking: You are the foreman, and the AI is rider Benito Cruz on the radio: stop the gather with short commands like ¡desmonta ya! and ¡aléjate de la cerca!, and plan where each rider will go using si + present → future (si escuchas truenos, bajarás…).

grammar.focus: Si + present → future; short radio or phone commands (si escuchas truenos, bajarás al arroyo; ¡desmonta ya!)

examples.es: Si ves relámpagos sobre la cresta, bajarás ya al terreno bajo.
examples.en: If you see lightning over the ridge, you'll go down to low ground right away.

examples.es: Si Lupe no contesta, Benito irá a buscarla por el lado norte.
examples.en: If Lupe doesn't answer, Benito will go look for her on the north side.

lessons.title: BQA Audit: Walking the Auditor Through Our Records
lessons.objective: Explain handling and treatment procedures formally to an auditor, and answer a question about a missing record.

words.note: Under the skin; the label says which route to use.

words.en: Good morning, Mr. Navarro; here are the treatment records.
words.es: Buenos días, señor Navarro; aquí tiene los registros de tratamiento.
words.note: Formal, to the auditor.

words.en: Each treatment is recorded the same day it is given.
words.es: Se registra cada tratamiento el mismo día que se aplica.

words.en: Each product is given according to the label or the vet's prescription.
words.es: Cada producto se aplica según la etiqueta o la receta veterinaria.

words.en: Injections are given in the neck, according to the BQA guidelines.
words.es: Las inyecciones se aplican en el cuello, según las guías BQA.

words.en: You're right; that line is missing the withdrawal date.
words.es: Tiene razón; a esa línea le falta la fecha de retiro.

words.en: It's calculated from the treatment date and the label.
words.es: Se calcula con la fecha de aplicación y la etiqueta.

words.en: That animal won't be sold until the date is confirmed.
words.es: Ese animal no se vende hasta que se confirme la fecha.
words.note: Hasta que + subjunctive for a future condition.

words.en: Would you like me to show you the corrective action in writing?
words.es: ¿Desea que le muestre la acción correctiva por escrito?
words.note: Formal: desea, le muestre.

lessons.speaking: You are the operation's manager, and the AI is BQA auditor Sr. Gerardo Navarro: walk him through how treatments are given and recorded, using usted and passive se (se registra cada tratamiento, se aplica según la etiqueta), and answer his questions about the logs.

grammar.focus: Formal register; passive se for procedures (se registra cada tratamiento; se aplica según la etiqueta)

examples.es: Se registra cada tratamiento con la fecha, la dosis y el número de lote.
examples.en: Each treatment is recorded with the date, the dose and the lot number.

examples.es: Los registros se revisan cada semana y se firman.
examples.en: The records are reviewed every week and signed.

lessons.title: Written Sick-Pen Report After a Pneumonia Outbreak
lessons.objective: Write a clear daily sick-pen report with treatments as the vet ordered, one death loss, and next steps.

words.note: In a report, write treatments as the vet ordered them, never as your own choice.
Standard written word for death loss in a report.
Agrees with the animal: novillo decaído, vaquilla decaída.

words.en: First, steer 318 died overnight in pen 4.
words.es: En primer lugar, el novillo 318 murió anoche en el corral 4.
words.note: Written register: open with en primer lugar and state the most serious fact first.

words.en: In addition, today we pulled five more steers with fever and cough.
words.es: Además, hoy apartamos cinco novillos más con fiebre y tos.

words.en: All of them were treated according to Dr. Herrera's written order.
words.es: Todos se trataron según la orden escrita del Dr. Herrera.

words.en: However, two steers still aren't responding to the antibiotic.
words.es: Sin embargo, dos novillos todavía no responden al antibiótico.

words.en: Therefore, we request a necropsy as soon as possible.
words.es: Por lo tanto, solicitamos una necropsia lo antes posible.
words.note: Formal written style; solicitamos sounds more professional than pedimos.

words.en: Each animal's temperatures are on the attached sheet.
words.es: Las temperaturas de cada animal están en la hoja adjunta.

words.en: I'll await your instructions for the two that aren't improving.
words.es: Quedo pendiente de sus indicaciones para los dos que no mejoran.
words.note: Formal closing to the vet.

words.en: Doña Ofelia, I'm sending you the full report by email.
words.es: Doña Ofelia, le envío el informe completo por correo.
words.note: Formal: Doña plus first name shows respect to the owner.

lessons.speaking: You are the foreman, and the AI is owner Ofelia Castañeda: read her your daily sick-pen report covering the treatments as the vet ordered, the overnight death in pen 4 and next steps, linking it with en primer lugar, además, sin embargo and por lo tanto.

grammar.focus: Written register; report connectors (en primer lugar, además, sin embargo, por lo tanto)

examples.es: En primer lugar, se encontró muerto el novillo 318 en el corral 4.
examples.en: First, steer 318 was found dead in pen 4.

examples.es: Sin embargo, los otros seis ya comen mejor; por lo tanto, seguimos el tratamiento indicado por el Dr. Herrera.
examples.en: However, the other six are eating better now; therefore, we're continuing the treatment Dr. Herrera ordered.

lessons.title: Texts and Calls: Washed-Out Road Delays the Shipment
lessons.objective: Text and call the buyer and the trucker to reschedule a shipment politely and confirm the new plan.

words.note: Many people just say el mensaje or el texto.

words.en: Good morning, Mr. Benavides, this is the ranch foreman writing.
words.es: Buenos días, Sr. Benavides, le escribe el capataz del rancho.
words.note: Formal text opening to the buyer: le escribe… identifies you politely.

words.en: The water took out the only road to the pens.
words.es: El agua se llevó el único camino a los corrales.

words.en: Would loading Thursday morning work for you?
words.es: ¿Le parecería bien cargar el jueves en la mañana?
words.note: Formal; the conditional softens the request.

words.en: Could you confirm by text before 5?
words.es: ¿Podría confirmarme por mensaje antes de las 5?
words.note: Formal.

words.en: Sorry for the trouble; the cattle are still in good shape.
words.es: Disculpe las molestias; el ganado sigue en buen estado.
words.note: Formal.

words.en: Ignacio, there's almost no signal here; can you hear me?
words.es: Ignacio, aquí casi no hay señal; ¿me escuchas?
words.note: Informal: tú with a trucker you work with often.

words.en: Could you bring the truck Thursday at 7?
words.es: ¿Podrías traer el camión el jueves a las 7?
words.note: Informal.

words.en: I'll text you the new time as soon as the grader comes through.
words.es: Te paso la nueva hora por mensaje en cuanto pase la motoniveladora.
words.note: Informal.

lessons.speaking: You are the foreman, and the AI is buyer Ricardo Benavides, then trucker Ignacio Robles: explain the washed-out road, propose a new shipping day and confirm the plan, using ¿le parecería bien…? and ¿podría confirmarme…? with the buyer and tú with the trucker.

grammar.focus: Phone and text conventions; conditional politeness (¿le parecería bien el jueves?, ¿podría confirmarme?)

examples.es: ¿Le parecería bien el jueves a las 8 de la mañana?
examples.en: Would Thursday at 8 in the morning work for you?

examples.es: Ignacio, ¿podrías confirmarme si tienes el camión libre el jueves?
examples.en: Ignacio, could you confirm whether your truck is free on Thursday?

lessons.title: Handing Back Custom-Grazed Cattle to Their Owner
lessons.objective: Walk a client through the season's results, explain one loss honestly, and set conditions for next year.

words.note: In the corral people often say se empanzó (it bloated).
Common ranch word for lighter cattle: becerros más livianos.

words.en: Mr. Cantú, I'm handing over 84 cows and 83 calves to you.
words.es: Señor Cantú, le entrego 84 vacas y 83 becerros.
words.note: Formal.

words.en: I'll be honest with you: we lost one calf to bloat.
words.es: Le voy a ser honesto: perdimos un becerro por timpanismo.

words.en: We found him dead in the low spot where the clover came up.
words.es: Lo encontramos muerto en el bajo donde creció el trébol.

words.en: The calves are coming in lighter because it rained very little.
words.es: Los becerros vienen más livianos porque llovió muy poco.

words.en: I understand you're upset, and your question is a fair one.
words.es: Entiendo su molestia, y su pregunta es muy válida.
words.note: Formal; acknowledges the client before explaining.

words.en: We'd take them next year as long as there's enough water.
words.es: Los recibiríamos el próximo año siempre que haya agua suficiente.
words.note: Siempre que + subjunctive sets a condition.

words.en: We'd keep the rate as long as you bring 90 pairs at most.
words.es: Mantendríamos la tarifa con tal de que traiga máximo 90 pares.

words.en: If you prefer, we'd go over the agreement together in March.
words.es: Si usted prefiere, revisaríamos el acuerdo juntos en marzo.
words.note: Formal.

lessons.speaking: You are the foreman, and the AI is owner Sr. Wilfredo Cantú: hand back his cattle, explain the lighter weaning weights and the calf lost to bloat honestly, and set terms for next year with the conditional and siempre que / con tal de que + subjunctive.

grammar.focus: Conditional; subjunctive in conditions (los recibiríamos otra vez siempre que el agua alcance)

examples.es: Aceptaríamos sus vacas otra vez siempre que el pozo tenga agua suficiente.
examples.en: We'd take your cows again as long as the well has enough water.

examples.es: Bajaríamos la carga animal a menos que llueva bien en la primavera.
examples.en: We would lower the stocking rate unless it rains well in the spring.

lessons.title: Capstone: A Shipping Day When Everything Goes Sideways
lessons.objective: Lead a full, difficult shipping day: train, solve problems, keep people safe, talk to outsiders, and report.

words.note: Weight cattle lose before weighing; buyers and sellers negotiate it.

words.en: Mateo, stand here and let them through one at a time.
words.es: Mateo, párate aquí y déjalos pasar de uno en uno.
words.note: Informal tú commands with a new hand.

words.en: Don't rush them; if they bunch up, step back.
words.es: No los apures; si se amontonan, retrocede un paso.

words.en: We stop the weigh-up until the technician calibrates the scale.
words.es: Paramos la pesada hasta que el técnico calibre la báscula.
words.note: Hasta que + subjunctive for a future event.

words.en: If it starts thundering, we stop everything and go to the trucks.
words.es: Si empieza a tronar, paramos todo y nos vamos a las trocas.

words.en: Mr. Carrillo, the head count matches the manifest.
words.es: Señor Carrillo, el total de cabezas coincide con el manifiesto.
words.note: Formal.

words.en: Don Ricardo, would you agree to wait until they calibrate the scale?
words.es: Don Ricardo, ¿estaría de acuerdo en esperar a que calibren la báscula?
words.note: Formal; conditional plus subjunctive.

words.en: Good thing you stayed calm with that steer, Mateo.
words.es: Qué bueno que te quedaste calmado con ese novillo, Mateo.
words.note: Informal praise.

words.en: In summary, 212 steers were shipped and nobody was hurt.
words.es: En resumen, se embarcaron 212 novillos y no hubo lesionados.
words.note: Written register for the day's report.

lessons.speaking: You are the foreman, and the AI plays hand Mateo Ruiz, inspector Luis Carrillo and buyer Ricardo Benavides: coach the sort with tú commands, keep the crew safe, answer the inspector, update the buyer with polite conditionals, and sum up the day with report connectors.

grammar.focus: Capstone: integrating the Master 20 grammar

examples.es: Mateo, no los apures; quiero que el aparte salga tranquilo.
examples.en: Mateo, don't rush them; I want the sort to go calmly.

examples.es: Si el técnico no llega a las 2, cargaremos mañana temprano.
examples.en: If the technician isn't here by 2, we'll load early tomorrow.
